meta.name: The Drip Fund
meta.tagline: Every dividend reinvests. More shares, more dividends, more shares. Slow, steady, relentless compounding. Water wears down stone.
meta.oneJob: A taxable brokerage account with one job: build a growing stream of passive dividend income to supplement retirement. Not the primary retirement vehicle (that's a 401k and Roth IRA) — this is the income supplement: money that shows up every month whether you work or not.
meta.riskTolerance: Moderate — sustainable, growing income over maximum yield
context: Home mortgage is being aggressively paid down — the retirement goal includes zero housing costs.
When the mortgage is paid off, a significant portion of freed cash flow redirects here immediately.
401k and Roth IRA are the primary retirement vehicles; this account is supplemental passive income.

strategyRules.title: DRIP is always on
strategyRules.body: Every dividend reinvests automatically. Never turn it off.

strategyRules.title: New money to the Core Three
strategyRules.body: All new contributions go to JEPI, JEPQ, SCHD only. No impulse buys.

strategyRules.title: Do not chase yield
strategyRules.body: If a yield looks too good to be true (15%+), it probably is.

strategyRules.title: Quality over quantity
strategyRules.body: Fewer, stronger positions beats 20 tiny ones.

strategyRules.title: Redirect mortgage cash flow
strategyRules.body: When the mortgage is paid off, redirect a significant portion of that freed cash flow here immediately.

strategyRules.title: Review quarterly
strategyRules.body: Confirm DRIP is active on all positions. No cash sitting idle in the money market unnecessarily.

strategyRules.title: Don't panic sell on dips
strategyRules.body: If the business is sound, a dip just means cheaper DRIP shares.

strategyRules.title: Tax awareness
strategyRules.body: This is a taxable account. Consider capital-gains implications before selling anything with large unrealized gains (especially AAPL).

strategyRules.title: Check SEC yield vs distribution yield
strategyRules.body: Before ever adding a position. If there's a huge gap, the 'income' is smoke and mirrors. See the QYLG lesson.

yieldTrap.warning: A high distribution yield reflects what was paid, not what will be paid. BDCs and struggling companies often show inflated yields precisely because the market is pricing in risk of cuts or collapse. Always ask: why is the yield this high? If the answer is 'the price has been falling for years,' that is a red flag, not a buying opportunity.
yieldTrap.examples: PSEC and OXSQ both destroyed capital while advertising double-digit yields.
yieldTrap.secLesson: Distribution yield includes option premiums and return of capital. SEC yield measures actual investment income. If a fund shows 19% distribution yield but 0.3% SEC yield, most of what it 'pays' you is your own money handed back in a different pocket — which is why the position loses value over time. Always compare both numbers before deciding.

holdings.risk: Mortgage REITs are interest-rate sensitive and have historically cut dividends. The high distribution yield warrants skepticism. Position is small (~$631). Watch Fed policy quarterly.

coreThree.note: All new monthly contributions split between these three. SCHD leads after the spring buys; JEPI has nearly caught JEPQ, so JEPQ is now the slightly underweighted one to favor next.

contribution.split: Roughly equal thirds into JEPI, JEPQ, SCHD; any extra to whichever is most underweighted.
contribution.tip: Fidelity allows dollar-based fractional purchases — type '$67' instead of a share count.

concentrationNotes.title: BP concentration (improving)
concentrationNotes.body: BP is now ~15% of the portfolio, down from ~20.3% in April — still the single largest position, but the plan to let other holdings grow and dilute it is visibly working. Do not add. The +$1,303 unrealized gain also makes selling tax-expensive. BP cut its dividend in 2020.

concentrationNotes.title: Covered-call concentration
concentrationNotes.body: The portfolio holds JEPI, JEPQ, and XYLD — three covered-call products (together about 29% of the account). In a strong bull market, covered calls cap upside. An accepted tradeoff for consistent monthly income.

concentrationNotes.title: NLY interest-rate risk
concentrationNotes.body: Mortgage REITs are rate-sensitive and have historically cut dividends. NLY's distribution yield is high enough to warrant skepticism. Position is small (~$631). Watch Fed policy quarterly.

projections.assumptions: Assumes 9% total annual return, 6% blended yield, starting value ~$22,000.
projections.caveat: These projections are optimistic. A covered-call-heavy portfolio may deliver yield but underperform on growth in strong bull markets. A more conservative, realistic target is roughly $400–500/month of income by year 10 at $300/month contributions.
